missing_supported_requirements.reason: Section discloses several climate metrics/targets, but it does not clearly link metrics to each sustainability-related risk/opportunity that could reasonably be expected to affect prospects (it reads as a climate metrics list rather than risk/opportunity-specific metric disclosure).
Metrics are presented, but not explicitly identified as the metrics used to measure/monitor each specific sustainability-related risk or opportunity (risk/opportunity mapping is missing).
Performance against targets is stated (e.g., '40.0% progress', 'on track'), but there is no analysis of trends or changes in performance (narrative trend analysis is absent).
No disclosure of revisions to targets (or an explicit statement that there were no revisions) and explanations for revisions.

No explicit statement that metric definitions/calculations are consistent over time, nor disclosure of how consistency is ensured; a Scope 1 correction is mentioned but not framed as consistency/redefinition handling.
Some targets are clearly labelled (e.g., TGT001), but others are generic ('All-scopes target') and not defined with clear, precise naming/description (baseline value lacks unit/context).

Comparatives are provided for financed emissions (2022–2024), but not for Scope 1, Scope 2, Scope 3 business travel, high-carbon exposure, internal carbon prices, carbon credits, or data-quality mix; paragraph B49 expects preceding-period comparatives for all amounts disclosed.
Section provides an estimation mix, but does not disclose revised comparative amounts when new information about prior-period estimates is identified (no revised comparatives shown).
No disclosure of the difference between previously disclosed and revised comparative amounts for any estimates.
No explanation of reasons for revising comparative amounts for estimates.
A correction to Scope 1 is described, but no revised comparative amounts are disclosed (or impracticability stated) in connection with any redefinition/replacement.
The Scope 1 correction is mentioned, but changes are not explained in a way that meets B52 (what changed in definition/approach, and what periods/metrics are affected).
No explanation of reasons for changes (including why the change provides more useful information) for any redefined/replaced metric.

If any metrics are newly introduced (e.g., carbon credit summary metric, internal carbon prices table, data-quality mix), no comparative amounts are provided and no impracticability statement is made.
No disclosure that revising comparatives is impracticable (if applicable). The section also does not address impracticability at all.
Section does not state that operational GHG emissions are measured in accordance with the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (or disclose an alternative required method).

Operational emissions tables provide limited measurement notes, but do not comprehensively disclose measurement approach, key inputs and assumptions for Scope 1/2/3 (e.g., organisational boundary approach for GHG Protocol, emission factors, activity data types).
No disclosure of why the chosen measurement approaches/inputs/assumptions were selected.
A Scope 1 correction is mentioned, but changes to measurement approach/inputs/assumptions and reasons are not clearly disclosed as required by 29(a)(iii)(3).
Section states a 'financial control' boundary, but does not disaggregate Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions between the consolidated accounting group and other investees as required.
No disaggregation of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions for other investees excluded from the consolidated accounting group.
No disaggregation for associates/joint ventures/unconsolidated subsidiaries (as applicable) within the Scope 1 and Scope 2 disclosure.

Location-based and market-based Scope 2 are disclosed and contractual instruments are mentioned, but the disclosure does not provide sufficient detail about contractual instruments (types, volumes, quality/attributes, how they affect market-based figure) to be 'necessary to inform users’ understanding'.

Scope 3 is not disclosed as a complete Scope 3 inventory with categories included; only business travel and financed emissions are shown, without stating which other Scope 3 categories are included/excluded.

required_fixes: Add explicit linkage of disclosed metrics/targets to the specific climate-related (and other sustainability-related, if applicable) risks and opportunities that affect prospects (IFRS S1.46).
For each target, add trend/change analysis (not just a single-year progress %) and disclose whether targets were revised; if none, state 'no revisions' (IFRS S1.51(f)–(g)).
Add preceding-period comparative amounts for all disclosed quantitative metrics (at least 2023 vs 2024), or explicitly state impracticability where applicable (IFRS S1.B49, B54).
If the Scope 1 'correction' affects prior periods, disclose revised comparative amounts, the differences, and reasons; if it does not, clarify that it relates only to 2024 and why (IFRS S1.B50–B52).

State the GHG measurement standard used (GHG Protocol Corporate Standard or jurisdictional alternative) and provide fuller disclosure of measurement approach, key inputs/assumptions, and reasons for choices; clearly describe changes made during the period and why (IFRS S2.29(a)(ii)–(iii)).

Provide required Scope 1/2 disaggregation between consolidated accounting group and other investees (associates/JVs/unconsolidated subsidiaries/other investees), or explicitly state not applicable with basis (IFRS S2.29(a)(iv)).
For Scope 3, disclose the Scope 3 categories included in the entity’s Scope 3 measure and clarify completeness (which categories are included/excluded) (IFRS S2.29(a)(vi)(1)).
Improve clarity/precision of target naming/definitions, especially the 'All-scopes target' (add unit, baseline year, target end-date/period, and clear description) (IFRS S1.53).
ifrs_coverage_judge.summary: The section provides several climate-related metrics (Scopes 1–3, financed emissions, high-carbon exposure, internal carbon pricing) and multiple targets with baselines and progress. However, it lacks required comparatives for most metrics, does not provide trend/change analysis or target revision disclosures, and does not meet key IFRS S2 GHG measurement disclosures (GHG Protocol statement, approach/inputs/assumptions and rationale, Scope 1/2 disaggregation, and complete Scope 3 category coverage). No invented missing-data language was detected.

unsupported_claims.location_in_section: Operational greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions → Operational emissions (tCO₂e) table (Scope 2 location-based row)
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The claims register marks this as supported, but the listed evidence_sources for CLM-MT-004 do not include the direct KPI value (e.g., reporting_kpis.scope2_location_2024_tco2e). Several cited paths are unrelated to Scope 2 location-based emissions. In the provided evidence_items, reporting_kpis.scope2_location_2024_tco2e exists and matches 6963.4977, but it is not actually referenced by the claim’s evidence_sources, so the support linkage is broken.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: Scope 3 emissions from business travel for 2024 were 289.9 tCO2e.
unsupported_claims.location_in_section: Operational greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions → Operational emissions (tCO₂e) table (Scope 3 business travel row)
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: The claims register marks this as supported, but the evidence_sources for CLM-MT-007 do not include the direct KPI value (e.g., reporting_kpis.scope3_travel_2024_tco2e). The cited sources are mostly target-scope fields and unrelated metadata. Although evidence_items include reporting_kpis.scope3_travel_2024_tco2e = 289.8833, it is not referenced by the claim’s evidence_sources, so the claim is not properly evidenced.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: For 2024, the bank held listed equity positions with market values of €23.93m, €556.40m, €35.36m, €79.11m, €25.57m, €1,886.33m, €2,564.65m, and €288.08m, using issuer revenue as the proxy input basis.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: CLM-MT-013 cites only financed_emissions_equity[5..7].market_value_meur as evidence, which covers only €1,886.33m, €2,564.65m, and €288.08m. It does not cite evidence for €23.93m, €556.40m, €35.36m, €79.11m, or €25.57m, nor does it cite proxy_basis/proxy input basis fields for all rows. Therefore the full multi-value claim is only partially evidenced.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: Target TGT001 covers all Kyoto 7 gases, is validated by SBTi, and 2024 progress is 40.0% with status "on track".
unsupported_claims.location_in_section: Target TGT001 — Scope 1 and Scope 2 absolute emissions reduction bullets
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: CLM-MT-019 evidence_sources only support the 40.0% progress (target_progress_pct_2024) and linkage (associated_gross_target_id). No evidence is provided for 'all Kyoto 7 gases', 'validated by SBTi', or the qualitative status 'on track'.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: Interim milestones for the financed emissions intensity target are 18.2 tCO2e per € million of lending in 2025 and 15.8 in 2028; the approach is a sectoral decarbonisation approach; validation is by UNEP FI; 2024 progress is 25.0%.
unsupported_claims.location_in_section: Scope 3 Category 15 financed emissions intensity reduction target bullets
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: CLM-MT-021 evidence_sources support milestones (interim_milestones_json) and 2024 progress (target_progress_pct_2024), but do not provide evidence for 'sectoral decarbonisation approach' or 'validated by UNEP FI'.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: An all-scopes (whole entity) target has a baseline value of 120,000.0, covers all Kyoto 7 gases, monitors progress as percentage reduction versus baseline, and reports 2024 progress of 13.3%.
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: CLM-MT-023 evidence_sources support baseline_value and 2024 progress (target_progress_pct_2024), but do not provide evidence for 'covers all Kyoto 7 gases' or the stated 'progress metric' definition (percentage reduction vs baseline).

questionable_claims.claim_text: Market-based Scope 2 is sourced directly from utility invoices and reflects grid emission factors adjusted for renewable energy certificates and power purchase agreements; certificates are not subtracted again during preparation to avoid double-counting.
questionable_claims.location_in_section: Operational emissions (tCO₂e) table notes (Scope 2 market-based row)
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Supported by metadata.scope2_rec_reconciliation, but it is a narrative control statement ('There is no double-counting') without showing reconciliation figures, REC/PPA volumes, or a documented calculation trail. Consider adding quantitative reconciliation or references to invoice totals/REC registry extracts.

questionable_claims.claim_text: Financed emissions are calculated using approaches aligned to the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) Standard.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Evidence relies on proxy_reason strings referencing PCAF sections, which indicates intent but is weaker than citing a formal methodology document, policy, or calculation workbook demonstrating alignment across asset classes.

questionable_claims.claim_text: Total loans were €31,150.64 million in 2022, 2023, and 2024.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Supported by financed_emissions[*].total_loans_meur, but the identical value across three years is unusual; may require an explanatory note (e.g., constant perimeter, restatement, or placeholder) to avoid credibility concerns.

required_fixes.fix: For Scope 2 location-based 2024 value, update CLM-MT-004 evidence_sources to include reporting_kpis.scope2_location_2024_tco2e (and/or the underlying calculation source).
For Scope 3 business travel 2024 value, update CLM-MT-007 evidence_sources to include reporting_kpis.scope3_travel_2024_tco2e (and/or the underlying travel-activity dataset).

For listed equity market values and proxy basis, either (a) cite evidence for all eight rows (financed_emissions_equity[0..7].market_value_meur and financed_emissions_equity[0..7].proxy_basis) or (b) narrow the claim to only the evidenced subset.
For TGT001, add evidence fields for gases covered (Kyoto 7), third-party validation (SBTi), and status ('on track'), or remove/qualify those statements.

For the Scope 3 Cat 15 intensity target, add evidence for 'sectoral decarbonisation approach' and 'validated by UNEP FI' (e.g., targets[1].approach, targets[1].validator) or remove/qualify those statements.
For the all-scopes target, add evidence for gases covered (Kyoto 7) and the progress metric definition, or remove/qualify those statements.

evidence_judge.summary: The section contains multiple numeric metrics that appear to have matching evidence in the provided evidence_items, but several claims are not properly supported because the claims register links to incorrect/insufficient evidence paths (notably Scope 2 location-based, Scope 3 business travel, and listed equity table completeness). Several target-related statements (Kyoto 7 coverage, third-party validation bodies, qualitative status, and stated approach) lack cited evidence. Fixing evidence linkages and adding explicit target metadata/validation fields (or qualifying/removing those statements) is required for approval.

voice_issues: Voice is generally neutral and formal, but it does not consistently use standards-oriented verbs (disclose, report, present) to frame metrics and targets.
Some phrasing is slightly narrative or conversational rather than definitional (e.g., 'For context on scale').
The section does not clearly distinguish between entity actions ('we' / the bank) and externally defined requirements, although it mostly avoids first person entirely.
structure_issues: Headings are not numbered and are not explicitly aligned to the IFRS pillar hierarchy (e.g., '4. Metrics and Targets', '4.1 Operational GHG emissions').
Most subsections lack a closing 'connectivity' sentence linking to related sections or financial statements, as required by the paragraph rules.

Several tables and lists are introduced with brief lead-ins, but there is no overarching section-level overview paragraph explaining the purpose of the Metrics and Targets section, the metric selection approach, or target-setting principles.
General sustainability metrics (IFRS S1) and climate-specific metrics (IFRS S2) are not clearly separated or labelled as such.
Methodology, boundary, data collection, estimation, and changes over time are partially described but not structured into a dedicated methodology/transparency block as recommended.

The 'All-scopes target (whole entity)' subsection does not clearly define the metric (e.g., units, boundary) and mixes baseline, progress metric, and carbon credit usage without the structured sequence boundary → inputs → calculation → outputs → limitations → governance.
wording_issues: Some sentences are longer and more complex than necessary, particularly in the description of market-based Scope 2 and PCAF methodology, and could be split for clarity.
The section occasionally uses explanatory or contextual language that is not strictly definitional (e.g., 'For context on scale'), which is slightly less standards-led.
The description of internal carbon pricing uses 'applies' but does not explicitly define the metric (e.g., 'Internal carbon price is defined as…') or clarify boundaries and limitations.
The 'All-scopes target (whole entity)' subsection uses generic wording ('baseline value') without specifying units or definition, which reduces precision and audit-readiness.

The final sentence on financed emissions intensity ('The bank also monitors a financed emissions intensity metric of 20.0 tCO₂e per € million.') is redundant and not clearly distinguished from the target baseline, which may cause confusion.
table_figure_issues: Tables do not have explicit numbers or captions (e.g., 'Table 4.1: Operational GHG emissions (tCO₂e)'), which is required for traceability and cross-referencing.
Tables are referenced in the narrative in a generic way ('are presented below') rather than by caption or number, which weakens traceability.

The repeated 'Investment decisions' row in the internal carbon pricing table may be a content issue, but from a style perspective it is not clearly distinguished (e.g., by sub-application or footnote), which can reduce clarity.
No assurance legend, data source type, or boundary notes are embedded in the tables, even though the style guide expects traceability metadata per row (definition, boundary, source type, mapping).
Figures are not used, which is acceptable, but there is also no explicit statement that figures are not required; however, this is a minor issue compared with missing captions and metadata.
required_fixes: Add a short section-level overview paragraph at the start of 'Metrics and Targets' that explains the purpose of the section, how metrics and targets are selected (materiality/relevance lens), and what they enable users to assess. Include a brief methodology/transparency paragraph covering boundaries, data sources, estimation, and update cadence.

Introduce a clear IFRS-aligned heading structure with numbering (e.g., '4. Metrics and Targets', '4.1 Reporting period and boundary', '4.2 Climate-related metrics (IFRS S2)', '4.3 Other sustainability-related metrics (IFRS S1)', '4.4 Targets and progress'). Ensure headings are consistently numbered and aligned to the pillar.

For each table, add a numbered caption and descriptive title (e.g., 'Table 4.1: Operational GHG emissions (tCO₂e), reporting year 2024, financial control boundary') and reference the table explicitly in the narrative (e.g., 'Table 4.1 presents…').

Refine long or complex sentences into shorter, definitional statements, especially in the Scope 2 market-based description and PCAF methodology bullets. Use constructions such as 'Metric is defined as…', 'Calculated using…', 'Includes…/Excludes…'.

Clarify and standardize the definition and units of the 'All-scopes target (whole entity)' metric. Explicitly state what the baseline value represents, the unit of measurement, the boundary, and how progress is calculated. Separate the description of carbon credit usage into a clearly labelled bullet (e.g., 'Planned use of carbon credits') and, if relevant, note limitations or assumptions.

Enhance traceability by adding, either in tables or in adjacent narrative, the source type (e.g., internal system, external data provider, estimation), boundary, and any assurance coverage for key metrics and targets, in line with the evidence and traceability rules.

Add brief closing 'connectivity' sentences at the end of major subsections (e.g., operational emissions, financed emissions, targets and progress) that link to related sections (e.g., Strategy, Risk Management) or to financial statement references using generic placeholders (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Strategy – Climate-related risks and opportunities]').

Where internal carbon pricing and financed emissions methodologies are described, explicitly distinguish between current-period facts (e.g., prices applied in 2024), estimation/judgement elements, and any forward-looking intentions (e.g., 'may be updated'), using cautious modality and standards-oriented verbs.

Remove or clarify redundant or potentially confusing statements, such as the final sentence on financed emissions intensity, by either integrating them into the target description with clear labelling or deleting them if duplicative.
style_judge.summary: The section is largely aligned with the desired formal, neutral, and metrics-focused style. It uses clear headings, structured bullets, and tables, and avoids promotional language. However, it does not fully meet the style guide requirements for IFRS-style structure and traceability: headings are unnumbered and not explicitly tied to IFRS pillars; tables lack numbered captions and explicit references; and there is no overarching methodology/approach narrative. Some wording is less definitional than preferred, and the 'All-scopes target' metric is not clearly defined. With targeted revisions to structure, table captioning, definitional clarity, and connectivity sentences, the section can be brought to full approval standard.
